Each agent identity must continuously answer random hardware-seeded timing challenges through its own physical sensor path; the orchestrator measures round-trip jitter against an ocean-crossing network baseline. A second gale-strength noise floor filters replay and simulation. Operators cannot fake distance: every additional identity needs its own sensor endpoint and low-jitter link, so each fake identity costs a dedicated device, power, and real round-trip budget. Residual submissions decay like a relic after missed challenge windows, expiring the identity.
